Ads do not penalize or downrank a game, an ad-acquired user is considered already acquired, and a drop in RFY impressions after advertising is not a penalty. Ad attribution credits plays and earnings for 30 days after a user's first join via an ad, and reports can lag up to 48 hours.
facts.quote: Engagement, retention, and monetization from users acquired through ads are excluded from RFY ranking signals.
facts.implication: Ads are useful for (a) measuring retention on a controlled cohort, (b) reaching the Kids/Select threshold and (c) seeding retrieval, but they cannot buy RFY rank. Ads Manager's own retention view (30-day attribution) is the way to read the paid cohort's D1/D7.

facts.claim: Non-staff DevForum replies report a minimum ad budget of 5 credits per day with at least 2 days (10 credits total) (July 19, 2026). A Jan 2026 reply says the UI recommends 16 credits/day. An April 2026 thread equates '10 ad credits per day' with '$10 USD or 2,850 Robux', and one commenter claims sponsored players give '20-30% worse stats' than algorithm players and that Roblox 'can take 1-3 weeks' before recommending a game.
facts.quote: The minimum ad budget is 5 Credits per day
facts.implication: These are working assumptions only: a first ad test might cost about $10-$100 over 2-7 days if 1 credit is about $1. Verify in the live Ads Manager UI before budgeting. Other threads: https://devforum.roblox.com/t/how-much-should-i-spend-on-ad-credits-for-a-test-run-of-my-game/4259529 and https://devforum.roblox.com/t/how-much-money-should-i-spent-to-get-into-the-algorithm/4551439

gaps: Roblox publishes NO numeric D1/D7/D30 or session-time benchmark values in its docs, newsroom or the benchmark-set announcement. The figures exist only inside the Creator Hub scorecards, which unlock at 100+ DAU. Typical vs successful official numbers could not be verified.

GameAnalytics' 2025 Roblox report does not define retention (classic vs rolling, denominator), so its ~4-11% median D1 cannot be reconciled with the DevForum/blog rule of thumb of 20-25% D1. The full PDF (investgame.net mirror) exceeded fetch limits and was not read.
No genre-specific (tycoon / incremental simulator / co-op) official retention benchmark was found. The RoWatcher tycoon ranges (D1 20-28%, D7 12-18%) have no stated methodology.
Competitor retention, revenue, payer conversion and developer-product (consumable) catalogs are not public. Only game passes and vote counts were retrievable from Roblox APIs.
Peak CCU figures come only from third-party trackers (e.g., RoWatcher's 30K peak for Flip a House!). Roblox's public API gives only the current 'playing' count (snapshot 2026-10-17).
It could not be verified whether Flip a House!, Renovate A House or other competitors have passed Kids/Select evaluation, i.e., whether they reach under-16 players.

RFY signal weights are published only as two priority tiers (most important / important), not numeric weights. The June 15, 2026 DevForum post's relative-importance chart is an image not readable as text.

The DevForum RFY announcement author (BurningEmbar) could not be confirmed as Roblox staff from page text, although it sits in the Announcements category. The same facts were taken from create.roblox.com docs instead.
The Discovery FAQ page shows no publication or last-updated date.

Official Ads Manager minimum daily budget, typical cost per play (Plays or Engagement objective) and the USD price of one ad credit are not published. The Robux-to-credit rate is only previewed in the UI. The community figures (5 credits/day x 2 days; ~$1 per credit) are unverified.
There is no official data on how long a typical new game takes to reach the 250 highly-engaged-player Kids/Select threshold, or what an Engagement-objective campaign costs to get there.
The date the expedited review fee changed from 100,000 Robux (June 16, 2026 post) to 50,000 Robux (current docs) was not found.
The URL and content of the 'Sketch Series: Onboarding Techniques' resource listed on the game-design hub were not retrieved.
Roblox's under-13 share of DAU was not extracted from the Q2 2026 letter. Only the 57% age-checked figure and the 'younger cohorts' monetization decline were confirmed.

The lensblox claim that the RFY change 'cost the company $9B' in market value is unsourced and was excluded. The causal link between the algorithm change and the stock drop is that author's interpretation.
